key_insight: A conditional diffusion model can generate realistic synthetic turbulent-flame evolution from experimental OH-PLIF and PIV data, including unseen transition events like liftoff and reattachment.
engineering_relevance: This offers a data-driven tool to augment scarce flame measurements and support combustion analysis, regime exploration, and model validation beyond traditional experiments and CFD.
method: Uses an x-prediction flow matching diffusion framework.
Combines a pixel-based spatiotemporal transformer with regime conditioning.
Synthesizes full space-time slabs and a transition-velocity model for controlled flame-state changes.
evidence_signal: The generated flames preserved key features and statistical consistency across space and time, especially at large scales, while transition synthesis produced spatiotemporally coherent liftoff and reattachment not seen during training.
watch_item: High-frequency temporal details and small-scale spatial structures can deviate from real data, and performance depends on the generated slab time span.
paper_title: Generating synthetic evolution of turbulent flames with an experimental data-based spatiotemporal diffusion model
